title: drift-check mutation matrix has no era-byte tamper class; era-flipped logs are accepted by replay_hashes (only the compare stage rejects them)
evidence:
harness/drift.odin — the six mutation classes (no era flip):
	// catalog_hash occupies bytes 17..24 (after magic4 + ver4 + seed8 + era1).
		append(&out, mutated(src, "catalog_hash", proc(b: []u8) { b[17] ~= 0xFF }))
		append(&out, mutated(src, "logic_hz", proc(b: []u8) { b[25] ~= 0x01 }))
		append(&out, mutated(src, "bad_magic", proc(b: []u8) { b[0] ~= 0xFF }))
		append(&out, mutated(src, "bad_version", proc(b: []u8) { b[4] = 99 }))
		append(&out, mutated(src, "bad_tag", proc(b: []u8) { b[41] = 0xFF }))
	append(&out, Mutation{label = "truncated", bytes = trunc[:]})
and drift_check asserts only acceptance:
		_, accepted := replay_hashes(tmp, cat, ticks, demo_spawns[:], demo_session, demo_qos, &fails)
harness/run.odin applies the tampered era without rejection at that stage:
	state.era = header.era // 3.1: the era rides the log header (it drives the director) — replay MUST apply it
detail: The era header byte became load-bearing in 3.1 (first era-3 golden); no drift mutation flips it. replay_hashes accepts era-tampered logs — only the manifest compare rejects them, which drift_check never runs. Verified: era 3→0 diverges at tick 1.
recommended_fix: Add an era_flip mutation (byte 16) and make drift_check compare replayed hashes against the manifest (as run_replay does), asserting the tamper diverges — currently it asserts only replay_hashes acceptance.
